title: κ = 0.4999 (+0.4963, +13,671.13% over #7000): OpenAI's tape multiplier gives log exponent 1/2 + ε for every fixed ε > 0
body: [OpenAI’s November 24 theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/math/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/paper.pdf) gives one deterministic multitape machine that computes the exact product of two $n$-bit integers in linear visited space. For **every fixed $\varepsilon>0$**, its worst-case time satisfies ```math T(n)=O_\varepsilon\!\left(n(\log n)^{1/2+\varepsilon}\right). ``` Here $\varepsilon$ measures the excess above the square-root logarithmic exponent. The same machine works for every fixed choice, although the implicit constant and threshold may depend on it. The open question is whether the residual factor above $n\sqrt{\log n}$ can be bounded by a constant. ## Result in the repository’s κ convention The repository measures the saving from exponent one. Setting $\varepsilon=1/2-\kappa$ gives $1/2+\varepsilon=1-\kappa$, so the bound covers every fixed $0<\kappa<1/2$. At the proposed witness **κ = 0.4999**, the target excess is **ε = 0.0001** and the logarithmic exponent is **0.5001**. OpenAI supplies the construction and its proof. This PR checks the machine contract, gives an explicit specialization, and proposes the resulting κ record for maintainer review. The local checks cover source integrity and exact parameter arithmetic. Independent compilation of the upstream Lean proof remains open. | Reference point | κ | Relative increase in κ at the proposed witness | |---|---:|---:| | [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) · selected frontier | 0.00363005817 | +13,671.13% | | [#8101](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8101) · conditional claim in the November 25 title survey | 0.003900866740647 | +12,715.10% | | **This PR** · numeric witness | **0.4999** | | | Supremum of the family; Weak ETH limit | 0.5 | not claimed | [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) is the maintainer-admitted conditional record at the pinned base revision. [#8101](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8101) was the newest open PR and the largest advertised conditional multiplication saving in a survey of 1,386 open PR titles on November 25, 2026. The survey distinguished claimed savings from ceilings and targets; it did not review the proof. The exponent saving increases by 0.49626994183 over [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) and by 0.495999133259353 over [#8101](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/8101). The percentages compare κ values, not measured running times. The November paper changes the overall construction and obtains logarithmic exponent $1/2+o(1)$ on one machine, with no complexity hypothesis. Its separate lower bound, which assumes variable-count Weak ETH, rules out every fixed κ > 1/2 ([step 4](#user-content-step-4-endpoint)). ## Significance for researchers The repository asks how much of the logarithmic factor an exact fixed-tape multiplier can save. Its October 9 [assembly-domain audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57/docs/research/assembly-domain-audit.md) identifies caps for the historical PR186 balanced assembly: $\kappa<1/33\approx0.0303$ from its retained range $a **Theorem (One multiplier for all lengths).** There is a deterministic multitape Turing machine that computes the full product of two $n$-bit integers in worst-case time at most $n(1+\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}$, visiting $O(n)$ tape cells. The three ideas below summarize the paper's introduction. They describe OpenAI's construction, not new work. **Sharing the movement.** On a power-of-two square array, transposition exchanges the row and column fields of the address. The paper splits each field into $m$ chunks and applies combinations of the $m$ chunk swaps to many independent streams at once. In a basis that diagonalizes every swap, the sign of their product is the parity of the number of $-1$ eigenvalues. A bulk-parity method from the companion Fourier paper computes that parity with a polynomial of degree $O(\sqrt{m\log m})$ and repairs the exceptional streams. This gives about $\sqrt{m\log m}$ stages, each linear in all $m$ swaps. Rectangular grouping lets several queries share a layout change. The resulting shifts take linear time, and the construction bounds the number of smaller interchanges per stream. **Sharing the arithmetic.** Many short, pairwise-coprime cyclic factors carry the digit convolution via the Chinese remainder theorem. Rather than padding each factor separately, a short transform borrows occupied coordinates and restores them. All the short transforms can then share one sequence of diagonal phases, address permutations and normalized Walsh transforms. With $O(\log n)$ bits per record, the accumulated error stays below one half. Rounding therefore recovers the exact coefficients before the carry scan. This gives a multiplier for each fixed exponent above 1/2 ([Multiplication at a fixed exponent](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/build/integers.tex)). **One machine.** A universal-search-style scheduler turns the family into a single program. It runs effectively generated candidates for target exponents $\theta_j=1/2+1/(j+2)$ on chunks of the operands. Allowances increase in a weighted diagonal order, and every attempt is fenced inside one linear space bound. A schoolbook multiplier is held in reserve. Every completed attempt is correct. For each fixed $j$, a suitable fixed chunk count eventually fits, and the scheduler incurs a constant-factor overhead for that attempt ([uniform multiplication proof](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/build/uniformity.tex)). ## From the theorem to κ ### 1. Match the machine contract | Repository requirement | Upstream statement | |---|---| | One deterministic machine; alphabet, tape count and transitions fixed before $n$ | One machine for all lengths, `UniformWorstCaseSpec` | | Two unsigned MSB-first $n$-bit operands, delimiter, leading zeros allowed | The same input encoding in the comparator specification | | Output is the full product in exactly $2n$ bits | The output tape holds a length-$2n$ string equal in value to the product | | One head per tape, moving at most one cell per step | Same step semantics | | Worst case over all inputs at each length | Maximum over actual halting traces at each positive width | Section-by-section comparison: [`PROOF.md` § Machine and output](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/research/nov24-direct-multiplication/PROOF.md#machine-and-output). ### 2. Specialize the quantifiers Fix $0<\kappa<1/2$ and set $g=1/2-\kappa$. Write the theorem's excess exponent as $\delta(n)\to0$. For all sufficiently large $n$, $\delta(n)\le g/2$, so ```math \tfrac12+\delta(n)\;\le\;\tfrac12+\tfrac g2\;<\;\tfrac12+g\;=\;1-\kappa . ``` At the witness $\kappa=4999/10000$, $g=1/10000$, and the eventual exponent $10001/20000$ is strictly below the target $5001/10000$. The bound holds for one fixed machine, not a family chosen per κ. ### 3. Change convention and absorb small lengths Replacing $1+\log n$ by the repository's $\max(1,\lceil\log_2 n\rceil)$ costs a constant factor for each fixed exponent. The finitely many lengths below the threshold have finite worst-case times, so a larger constant covers every $n\ge1$. ### 4. Leave the endpoint open An excess exponent that tends to zero can still contribute an unbounded factor, such as a power of $\log\log n$, so the theorem does not give κ = 1/2. The selected record stores the open interval `(0, 1/2)` with the exact witness `4999/10000`. The verifier rejects 1/2 and every value above it. Every fixed κ with 0.4999 < κ < 0.5 already follows from the same theorem, so there is no largest supported witness. Choosing 0.499999 would instantiate another consequence of the theorem, not a new algorithm. The κ-dependent constants and thresholds do not justify a moving target κ(n) that approaches 1/2 at a prescribed rate. Above the endpoint, the paper's lower bound requires $\Omega(n\sqrt{\log n})$ worst-case time at every sufficiently large length from every exact deterministic multitape multiplier. That excludes every fixed κ > 1/2. The bound assumes variable-count Weak ETH: no deterministic algorithm decides 3-SAT in time $2^{O(v^{1-\eta})}L^{O(1)}$ for any fixed $0<\eta<1$, where $v$ is the number of variables and $L$ the input length. This is weaker than ordinary ETH, since it permits a $2^{O(v/\log v)}$ algorithm. The upper claim does not use it. ## Explicit construction at κ = 0.4999 [`CONSTRUCTION.md`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/research/nov24-direct-multiplication/CONSTRUCTION.md) specializes the paper's fixed-candidate construction at the selected witness. The following choices fit that construction and its uniform scheduling framework: | Choice | Exact value | Meaning | |---|---:|---| | Selected saving κ | `4999/10000` | Required logarithmic exponent `5001/10000` | | Candidate index j | `19998` | θ_j = 1/2 + 1/(j+2) | | Candidate exponent θ_j | `10001/20000` | 0.50005, strictly below the target 0.5001 | | Fourier/interchange exponent ρ | `20001/40000` | Slack for the fixed logarithmic factors | | Intermediate interchange exponent γ | `40001/80000` | Strictly between 1/2 and ρ | | Interchange label prime p | `240007` | Admissible prime for the label construction | The replay checks that p is prime, the exponent ordering and the exact positive margin: ```math \gamma-\left(\frac12+\frac{3p-1}{p^2}\right) =\frac{1760049}{4608268803920000}>0, \qquad \frac12<\gamma<\rho<\theta_j<1-\kappa. ``` The note follows each stage in turn: digit packing, short cyclic axes, CRT order changes, synchronized Fourier/Walsh layers, certified precision, coefficient rounding and carry output. For each stage it identifies the recurrence, movement and visited-space bounds used. This fixed candidate alone suffices for κ = 0.4999. The paper's single scheduler supplies the stronger simultaneous statement for every fixed κ < 1/2. These are compatible choices for the paper's effective construction, not constants extracted from an upstream executable. The finite interchange and Walsh templates, precision constants, chunk count and complete transition table have not been generated. Their existence and the all-width bounds come from the cited construction. The new checks establish that the displayed parameters are admissible. They do not execute a multiplier or discharge the remaining template obligations. ## What changes in the repository | Area | Change | |---|---| | [`certificates/selected-result.json`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/certificates/selected-result.json) | Selects `4999/10000` with `supported_savings = (0, 1/2)` and no assumptions; `previous_record` points to the [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) checkpoint | | [`certificates/nov24-direct/`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/tree/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/certificates/nov24-direct) | Claim with exact construction parameters, source manifest and validation scope | | [`research/nov24-direct-multiplication/`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/tree/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/research/nov24-direct-multiplication) | Proof and construction notes; eight unmodified upstream files with Git blob IDs and SHA-256 digests | | [`certificates/checkpoints/frontier7000.json`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/certificates/checkpoints/frontier7000.json) | Byte-exact [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) record, replayable with its original verifier | | Status docs, task picker, sparse-baseline helper, Makefile, CI | Status and CI navigation updated; direct task-picker routes validated, including sparse omissions; sparse-baseline helper routed to the direct verifier; all required workflow triggers covered; historical replay kept through the checkpoint wrapper | ## Verification The branch is based on canonical main at `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` (priority revision 8). It needs only the Python standard library and runs offline. ```sh make nov24-direct-verify # direct corollary python3 -B scripts/verify_nov24_direct.py --kappa 499999/1000000 # another fixed witness below 1/2 python3 -B scripts/replay_frontier7000_checkpoint.py --check-only # predecessor record ``` - **Direct corollary and parameters.** The eight archived upstream files match a fresh fetch of commit `92b516ef` byte for byte and by Git blob and tree identity. The offline replay checks the retained fingerprints without contacting upstream. It also checks the comparator binding: the comparator names `OAI.Computability.NearSquareRoot.uniformIntegerMultiplication` in solution module `OAI.Computability.NearSquareRoot.Main`. The remaining checks cover the candidate index, the strict exponent ordering, the primality of p, the exact label margin, the rational specialization and the empty assumption list. - **Rejection controls.** From a clean export of the committed direct source closure, the verifier rejects κ = 1/2, κ = 5001/10000 and a one-byte change to the archived `Main.lean`. It accepts 4999/10000 and 499999/1000000. - **Predecessor.** In an isolated tree, the [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) checkpoint passes its original verifier, `PASS_FRONTIER7000_BINDINGS_AND_RECORDED_EVIDENCE`. This check confirms the bindings and recorded evidence. It is not a new scientific replay. - **Repository checks.** `check_selected_ci_inputs.py --require-triggers` passes with 22 required paths and no uncovered push or pull-request inputs. `git diff --check` and four test modules pass: `test_nov24_direct.py` (9 tests), `test_research_baseline_sparse.py` (12), `test_research_priority_context.py` (13) and `test_research_current_status.py` (6). The new tests reject composite label parameters, inconsistent candidates, zero slack, source tampering, unsupported endpoints and false execution claims. The picker tests cover missing and sparse direct entry points. - **Earlier broad-suite review.** Before this rebase, a review of the earlier local head `de3319005` recorded 764 discovered tests, 23 of them skipped. Its remaining failures came from one unchanged fixture absent from the partial checkout; restoring its committed bytes gave a passing 14-test rerun. These are prior-revision results. Fresh verification of this revision is the focused coverage above. Neither a complete all-green run nor a hosted CI run is claimed. - **Not run.** The upstream Lean dependency graph was not built, the comparator was not executed, the finite templates were not generated and no multiplier was run. The complete historical [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) scientific replay was not rerun. The local replay covers source integrity, scalar construction parameters and the corollary. It does not independently re-establish the theorem. **Where to start reading** - [`CONSTRUCTION.md`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/research/nov24-direct-multiplication/CONSTRUCTION.md): explicit candidate choices, construction stages and remaining finite-template work. - [`PROOF.md`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/research/nov24-direct-multiplication/PROOF.md): model comparison, quantifiers, endpoint and attribution. - [`intro.tex`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/build/intro.tex): the upper and lower theorem statements and the model. - [`uniformity.tex`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/build/uniformity.tex): the single-machine scheduler. - [`NearSquareRootMultiplication.lean`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/ComparatorChallenges/NearSquareRootMultiplication.lean) and [`Main.lean`](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/OAI/Computability/NearSquareRoot/Main.lean): the formal specification and proof entry. - [`scripts/verify_nov24_direct.py`](https://github.com/zxv/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/nov24-retained-kappa-003/scripts/verify_nov24_direct.py): the replay. ## Scope - **Construction and attribution.** This is an explicit κ claim obtained by specializing OpenAI's multiplication construction. This PR contributes the construction specialization and dependency account, contract comparison, exact parameter checks, selection record and integration. The underlying algorithm and upstream proof remain attributed to OpenAI. - **Unconditional upper bound.** The upper theorem uses no Weak ETH or other complexity hypothesis, so the record lists no assumptions. Only the paper's separate lower bound depends on Weak ETH. - **Not independently formalized.** Upstream provides a Lean proof and comparator configuration. Neither was built or run here. - **Endpoint not claimed.** κ = 1/2 is outside the claim and is rejected by the verifier. - **Changes the selected frontier.** Merging requires maintainer authorization. The [#7000](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7000) record and its replay stay available as a checkpoint. ## Open next questions - **The endpoint.** Can one fixed-tape machine reach $O(n\sqrt{\log n})$? Deriving that from the present estimate needs $(1+\log n)^{\delta(n)}=O(1)$; $\delta(n)\to0$ alone does not suffice. A different construction could settle the endpoint independently. - **Materialize the construction.** Generate the finite templates and their exact child bills. Then compile their movement, precision, restoration and scheduling operations faithfully into the tape model. The construction note lists these remaining tasks. - **Independent formal replay.** Build the upper comparator at `92b516ef` and record its accepted declarations and actual axioms, following the [upstream comparator instructions](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/ComparatorChallenges/README.md). - **Repository direction.** The proposed witness lies exactly 10⁻⁴ below 1/2. The task catalogue should weigh endpoint, formal-replay and lower-bound work against further grouped-assembly refinements. None of these questions is used to justify the selected claim. ## Literature 1. **OpenAI** (2026). “The logarithmic exponent of integer multiplication on tapes.” Preprint, November 24, 2026. [release `92b516ef`](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026) The entire scientific input. The uniform multiplication theorem supplies the selected claim. The upper estimate leaves endpoint attainment open. Under variable-count Weak ETH, the multiplication lower bound also excludes every fixed saving above 1/2. The paper also gives one-machine, linear-space upper bounds of the same form for exact division with remainder and the floor integer square root, each with a conditional $\Omega(n\sqrt{\log n})$ lower bound. Those corollaries are outside this certificate, and upstream lists them as unformalized. [Paper corollaries](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-integer-multiplication-on-tapes-November-24-2026/build/uniformity.tex) · [Formalization scope](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/docs/379.md) 2. **OpenAI** (2026). Lean formalization `OAI.Computability.NearSquareRoot` and comparator challenge `NearSquareRootMultiplication`. [proof entry](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/OAI/Computability/NearSquareRoot/Main.lean) · [specification](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/92b516ef8e2abf66c3db7aa31438d3010bc7956f/lean/ComparatorChallenges/NearSquareRootMultiplication.lean) Used to compare the machine contract field by field and to bind the theorem name. It was archived and hashed here but not built. 3. **David Harvey and Joris van der Hoeven** (2025). “Integer multiplication is at least as hard as matrix transposition.” arXiv:2503.22848. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.22848) The paper's lower bound transfers transposition hardness to multiplication through this reduction. It is context for the endpoint and is not used in the upper claim. 4. **Leonid A. Levin** (1973). “Universal sequential search problems.” *Problems of Information Transmission* 9(3). [Math-Net.Ru](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/ppi914) The paper's single machine schedules its candidates as in universal search.
